==¶ THE EPISTLE OF PAVL <br>the Apoſtle to the Philippians.==
{{rule}}

==={{Chapter|1|CHAP. I.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#1:3|3]] He teſtifieth his thankefulneſſe to God, and his loue toward them, for the fruits of their faith and fellowſhip, in his ſufferings, [[#1:9|9]] dayly praying to him for their increaſe in grace: [[#1:12|12]] Hee ſheweth what good the faith of Chriſt had receiued by his troubles at Rome, [[#1:21|21]] and how ready he is to glorifie Chriſt either by his life or death, [[#1:27|27]] exhorting them to vnitie, [[#1:28|28]] and to fortitude in perſection.}}

{{Verse|1|1|notext=}}{{dropinitial|P|image=King James Bible (1611) page A3r (P).png|imgsize=100px}}Aul and Timotheus the ſeruants of Ieſus Chriſt, to all the Saints in Chriſt Ieſus, which are at Philippi, with the Biſhops and Deacons:

{{Verse|1|2}} Grace {{smaller|be}} vnto you, and peace, from God our Father, and {{smaller|from}} the Lord Ieſus Chriſt.

{{Verse|1|3}} I thanke my God vpon euery ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, mention.''}} remembrance of you,

{{Verse|1|4}} Alwayes in euery prayer of mine for you all making requeſt, with ioy

{{Verse|1|5}} For your felowſhip in the Goſpel from the firſt day vntill now;

{{Verse|1|6}} Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you, ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=''Or, will finiſh it.''}} will performe {{smaller|it}} vntil the day of Ieſus Chriſt:

{{Verse|1|7}} Euen at it is meete for mee to thinke this of you all, becauſe I ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, you haue me in your heart.''}} haue you in my heart, in as much both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the Goſpel, ye all are ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, partakers with me of grace.''}} paratakers of my grace.

{{Verse|1|8}} For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all, in the bowels of Ieſus Chriſt.

{{Verse|1|9}} And this I pray, that your loue, may abound yet more & more in knowledge, and in ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, ſense.''}} iudgment.

{{Verse|1|10}} That ye may ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, trie''}} approue things that ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, differ.''}} are excellent, that ye may be ſincere, and without offence till the day of Chriſt.

{{Verse|1|11}} Being filled with the fruites of righteouſneſſe, which {{smaller|are}} by Ieſus Chriſt vnto the glory and praiſe of God.

{{Verse|1|12}} But I would yee ſhould vnderſtand brethren, that the things {{smaller|which}} {{smaller|happened}} vnto mee, haue fallen out rather vnto the furtherance of the Goſpel.

{{Verse|1|13}} So that my bonds ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, for Chriſt.''}} in Christ, are manifeſt in all the ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, Cæſars Court.''}} palace, and in ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, to all others.''}} all other {{smaller|places.}}

{{Verse|1|14}} And many of the brethen in the Lord, waxing confident, by my bonds, are much more bold to ſpeake the word without feare.

{{Verse|1|15}} Some in deed preach Chriſt, even of enuie and ſtrife, and ſome alſo of good will.

{{Verse|1|16}} The one preach Chriſt of contention, not ſyncerely, ſuppoſing to adde affliction to my bonds:

{{Verse|1|17}} But the other of love, knowing that I am ſet for the defence of Goſpel.

{{Verse|1|18}} What then: Notwithstanding euery way, whether in pretence, or in trueth: Chriſt is preached, and I therein doe reioyce, yea, and will reioyce.

{{Verse|1|19}} For I know that this ſhall turne to my ſaluation through your prayer, and the ſupplie of the ſpirit of Ieſus Chriſt,

{{Verse|1|20}} According to my earneſt expectation, and {{smaller|my}} hope, that in nothing I ſhalbe aſhamed: but {{smaller|that}} with all boldnes, as alwayes, {{smaller|ſo}} now alſo Chriſt ſhal be magnified in my body, whether {{smaller|it}} {{smaller|be}} by life or by death.

{{Verse|1|21}} For to me to liue {{smaller|is}} Chriſt, and to die {{smaller|is}} gaine.

{{Verse|1|22}} But if I liue the in fleſh, this is the fruit of my labour: yet what I ſhal chuſe, I wote not.

{{Verse|1|23}} For I am in a ſtrait betwixt two, hauing a deſire to depart, ⁊ to bee with Chriſt, which is farre better.
